twins.label: NASA Twins Study — ISS one-year mission
twins.timing_source: Public mission record (Soyuz TMA-16M launch / TMA-18M landing); not contained in the TERRA data file.
twins.phase_convention: Flight split into thirds (early/mid/late), the convention used by the combined radiation report; not a NASA-defined phase boundary.

inspiration4.label: SpaceX Inspiration4 (3-day free-flyer, ~585 km)
inspiration4.timing_source: Public mission record; the CBC file gives only L-/R+ day labels, so sample clock times are unknown.

sources.title: NASA RadLab — ISS DosTel1/DosTel2
sources.note: 585,235 rows bundled (accessed 2026-11-14). Absorbed dose rate, µGy/h, area monitors in the Columbus module — not personal dosimeters.

sources.title: RadLab API documentation
sources.note: Returned HTTP 500 on 2026-11-15. Units are carried from the bundled 2026-11-14 export query (absorbed_dose_rate, µGy/h).

sources.title: Inspiration4 whole blood / CBC — NASA OSDR OSD-569 (LSDS-7)
sources.note: 4 crew (C001–C004), L-92, L-44, L-3, R+1, R+45, R+82, R+194. WBC in thousand/µL (= 10⁹/L); differentials in cells/µL; lab ranges per row. No in-flight samples, no TERRA.

sources.title: Al-Turki et al. 2024, Commun Biol — TERRA increases in response to spaceflight
sources.note: Supplementary Data 2, subject TW, UUAGGG normalized abundance (8 in-flight, 3 post-flight). Paper: in vitro ionizing radiation increased TERRA; simulated microgravity did not.

sources.title: NASA Twins Study (PMC7580864)
sources.note: Reports a physical dosimeter dose of 76.18 mGy and an effective dose of 146.34 mSv for the one-year mission.

sources.title: Crucian et al. 2015 — Alterations in adaptive immunity persist during long-duration spaceflight (PMC5515498)
sources.note: n=23 ISS crew. Samples L-180, L-45, ~FD14, months 2–4, ~6 months, 3 h after landing (R+0), R+30. L-180 used as baseline because later pre-flight samples may reflect pre-mission stress. WBC and granulocytes rose in flight; lymphocytes/monocytes unaltered; landing surge attributed in literature to stress-induced neutrophil demargination. Values are only in figures (not tabulated) — no absolute counts are imported.

sources.title: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 — 4.8 Ionizing radiation
sources.note: Career limit: total career effective dose < 600 mSv (NASA effective dose, NASA Q, 2012 cancer model). Table 4.8-1: blood-forming organs 250 mGy-Eq (30-day), 500 mGy-Eq (1-year). The combined report’s “250 mSv per event” paraphrase does not match this table’s quantity or units.

sources.title: NASA radiation research reference (NTRS 20160009163)
sources.note: PDF reachable (8 MB). Not machine-parsed in this build; no values are taken from it.

sources.title: NASA Twins Study collection timeline (NTRS 20160012724, slide 24)
sources.note: Used for FD→calendar mapping of TERRA samples (dates only; clock times not verified).

sources.title: NOAA solar proton event catalog (hosted by NASA)
sources.note: GOES >10 MeV proton flux (pfu). Not ISS dose.

sources.title: combined_radiation_report.pdf (team-supplied)
sources.note: Illustrative projections. 340-day constant-rate total (625.60 mSv) and the 6-month biological projection (≈335 mSv) use different durations and are not merged. Radiation shares (60/10/0%) are adjustable assumptions.

Effective dose as reported by NASA in the source; method per source.

records.definition: Published cohort finding (n=23 ISS crew), paired comparison with L-180 baseline.
records.observed_change: Absolute WBC and granulocytes higher than L-180 during flight (significant at early and late timepoints); lymphocytes and monocytes unaltered.
records.suggested_action: Context only; compare individual results with personal baseline.

records.definition: WBC surge after landing (sample ~3 h after landing).
records.observed_change: WBC elevated at R+0 relative to baseline.
possible_contributors: Stress-induced neutrophil demargination (cited by the authors)
records.suggested_action: Interpret landing-day WBC with landing timing in mind.

records.observed_change: The study used L-180 as baseline because samples collected closer to launch may be influenced by pre-mission stress.
records.suggested_action: Use an early pre-flight baseline window.

records.observed_change: WBC at L-3 exceeded L-44 in all four crew (7.0 vs 5.5; 7.2 vs 5.4; 9.8 vs 9.3; 10.6 vs 6.4 ×10⁹/L).
possible_contributors: Training, travel, sampling time of day

records.observed_change: In vitro ionizing radiation (2 Gy γ-rays) increased TERRA transcription; simulated microgravity did not.
records.suggested_action: Supports radiation as a candidate contributor; does not establish dose-response in astronauts.

records.observed_change: No bundled dataset contains a pre-flight TERRA rise; this is modeled as an adjustable stress contribution.
records.suggested_action: Test with pre-flight serial TERRA samples before relying on it.

report_projection.label: Combined report — deep-space projection at 1.84 mSv/day (illustrative; read by eye ±5 pp)
report_projection.note: Illustrative model output, not measured deep-space astronaut data. Radiation shares (TERRA 60%, WBC/granulocytes 10%, lymphocytes 0%) and post-flight fractions are adjustable assumptions. No landing-day TERRA value exists in the report.
